text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent weekly newspapers The Guardian and Mmegi (The Reporter) on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Three men shot at Botswana soldiers on anti-poaching patrols on Sedudu Island in the Chobe river on the Namibian border on Monday. The fire was not returned but a rocket flare was set up to illuminate the area forcing the men to flee. The ownership of Sedudu Island is disputed by Namibia and Botswana. The issue has to be resolved to determine the position of the border between the two countries and has been referred to the International Court of Justice at The Hague.

- Doubts are cast on a proposed $7.0 billion oil-from-coal project and a refinery, which South African Jan Visser says he is to set up in Botswana, through his Universal Investments company. Visser talks about listing the project on the Botswana Stock Exchange, which would increase the market capitalisation of the exchange by 18 times. The investment would be equal to 50 per cent of Botswana's yearly Gross Domestic Product and the gross revenue equal to seven per cent of GDP.
- Relatives of three Batswana men who have not been seen since they were detained by the South African Police in 1976, are to apply to the South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

- The loss making Botswana Housing Corporation, recommended in a recent report by the private sector as a candidate for privatisation, has been urged in an internal report to shed 490 of its 1041 employees.
